steps.message: For Calvin Klein: For Q1 2026, show qualifying revenue, item count, items with a known sale price, items with a missing sale price, distinct orders, distinct customers, and AOV. Define AOV as SUM(sale_price) divided by every distinct qualifying order, including orders containing a missing-price item. Also show SUM(sale_price) restricted to missing-price items. Explain how SQL NULL statuses and NULL prices affect these results; do not treat unknown prices as free purchases.

facts.denominator: distinct qualifying orders in the same scope and period

facts.entity: qualifying Q1 items with missing sale_price only

criteria.description: State only supported observations. Treat causal explanations as unverified hypotheses unless the observed data establish them.

Exclude NULL item/order statuses under SQL three-valued logic. Count a qualifying NULL-price item/order/customer while SUM ignores its unknown price. The all-NULL subset SUM is NULL, not zero; do not claim missing prices are free purchases.

turn-1.reference_answer: Calvin Klein Q1 qualifying revenue was 798 from 23 items: 22 had a known sale price and 1 had a missing price. There were 21 distinct orders and 13 distinct customers. Under the requested denominator, AOV was 798 / 21 = 38.00. SUM(sale_price) over only the missing-price items is NULL, not zero. NULL item or order statuses fail the qualifying NOT IN predicates; a qualifying NULL-price item remains in counts but contributes no known amount to SUM. Its price is unknown, not free.
turn-1.reference_procedure: Query the scoped sales relation for Q1 aggregates with COUNT(*), COUNT(sale_price), COUNT(*)-COUNT(sale_price), distinct order/customer IDs, and SUM(sale_price)/COUNT(DISTINCT order_id). Separately aggregate SUM(sale_price) WHERE sale_price IS NULL. Compare missing-status counts in transactions and sales to verify that the NULL-status rows are excluded; do not assume an undocumented source transformation.
